meta.title: quality-gates roadmap — the repo dogfooding its own audit plugin

buildCommands.selftests: for f in $(find plugins/audit/hooks plugins/audit/scripts -name '*.py' | sort) $(find plugins/audit/tests -name '*.py' | sort); do python3 "$f" --selftest || exit 1; done
buildCommands.plugin-validate: claude plugin validate . && claude plugin validate plugins/audit
buildCommands.sweep: for f in $(find plugins/audit/hooks plugins/audit/scripts -name '*.py' | sort) $(find plugins/audit/tests -name '*.py' | sort); do python3 "$f" --selftest >/dev/null || { echo "FAIL $f"; exit 1; }; done
buildCommands.lint: ruff check plugins/audit tools && vermin -t=3.8- --no-tips --violations plugins/audit/scripts plugins/audit/hooks plugins/audit/tests

phases.title: CI legs: Windows separators + Linux viewport
CRLF: the assets' eol is a contract

bugs.title: audit.md YAML frontmatter silently dropped at runtime
bugs.description: audit.md's frontmatter description contained ': ' unquoted, so YAML parsing failed and Claude Code loaded the command with EMPTY metadata — description, argument-hint and allowed-tools never applied, since v0.2.0. init.md's argument-hint parsed as a YAML array instead of a string.
repro: observe: 'YAML frontmatter failed to parse ... loads with empty metadata'
bugs.expected: All four commands load with their declared metadata.
bugs.actual: audit.md loaded with empty metadata; init.md argument-hint was an array.
bugs.notes: Found by adopting claude plugin validate as a release gate; the gate is now enforced in CI.

bugs.title: journal_dir returns mixed path separators; j12 red on Windows
bugs.reportedBy: CI run 31427419994 (first Windows leg over the v0.29+ backlog)
bugs.description: scripts/audit-journal.py journal_dir() joins the project root with config-derived forward-slash components (os.path.dirname of manifestPath), returning e.g. C:\tmp\x\docs/audit\journal on Windows. hooks/_config.py j12 compares str(Path(answer)) == answer, which fails on the separator spelling alone. Same path, two spellings; also yields proj/./journal on POSIX when the manifest sits at the project root.
bugs.expected: journal_dir returns one normalized spelling on every platform.
bugs.actual: Mixed separators on Windows; a redundant ./ segment on POSIX with a root manifest.
bugs.notes: Fix the class: normalize at the API, not at the comparison.

bugs.title: panel policy view exceeds the 1560px capture viewport on Linux
bugs.description: capture-screenshots.mjs --check: the policy view renders 1590px tall in a 1560px viewport on ubuntu (Linux font metrics run taller than macOS), so the sticky save bar would cover table rows in a capture. The check's own comment prescribes the fix: raise the viewport.
repro: node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs --check  (on ubuntu: FAIL the policy view is 1590px tall...)
bugs.expected: The policy view fits the capture viewport on every CI platform.
bugs.notes: Viewport is the lever the check names; 1680 leaves margin.

bugs.title: ui/ assets CRLF-converted on Windows checkout; cross-line pins fail
bugs.reportedBy: CI run 31428171362 (Windows leg, after BF1 fixed j12)
bugs.description: scripts/ui/* are byte-precise build inputs read with newline='' (deliberate: the assembled UI_HTML/_CSS/_SCRIPT byte-identity depends on exact bytes). With no .gitattributes, windows-latest checkout (autocrlf) rewrites them to CRLF, so every selftest pin that spans a line boundary fails (panel-server: 'four sections are ONE list', 'wide data table scrolls'; render-report would fail the same way - the sweep stops at the first red).
repro: fresh checkout with core.autocrlf=true; python plugins/audit/scripts/panel-server.py --selftest
bugs.expected: Assets reach every platform LF, and a CRLF asset is named by a selftest, not discovered via a distant pin.
bugs.actual: CRLF assets on Windows; two cross-line pins red; the real cause two files away from the failure.
bugs.notes: Fix the class: eol contract in .gitattributes + a named LF guard beside each reader.

bugs.title: sub-cent cost rule proven one module away from where it renders
bugs.reportedBy: P13.3 mutation pass (recorded as F10 in the private fault ledger)
bugs.description: Corrupting _report_usage's fmt_cost delegation and rerunning its own selftest stayed green - no fixture in that suite spends under a cent, so the <$0.01 rule is exercised only in _fmt's goldens. The consumer could stop delegating (or mangle the arguments) and its 49 cases would not notice; the parallel fmt_tokens mutation goes red in three cases by name, which is what the cost side should look like.
repro: weaken _fmt.fmt_cost delegation in _report_usage; python3 plugins/audit/scripts/report/_report_usage.py --selftest stays green
bugs.expected: A sub-cent spend asserted through the rendered tile string in _report_usage's own suite.
bugs.actual: Delegation-coverage gap; the rule is proven only where it is defined, not where it renders.
bugs.notes: The F3/u8 class one level down: green for the wrong reason.
